expectation: small: in the development labels the levels differ on about 56 of 692 pairs, so the feature can only move a few decisions
known_risks: development labels include the X1 and near-miss packs, so they are no longer test sets
the pack is a stress set, not the engine's review band (that band is used up in these states); coverage here does not predict coverage in production
drift pairs show the shared source id, so their labels lean on it
the near-miss development pairs were labelled with the engine's 'different' visible
level_woe_source: x3_level.level_woe: m from GRID3/HFR twins sharing a source id, u from each GRID3 facility against one random other HFR facility in its LGA (random.Random(0), sorted globalid order); 34 states other than Edo, Kano and Ondo; no review label
question: Does the registries' facility level (GRID3 facility_level, HFR type) add to the pair decider, refitted on the recheck-corrected labels?

arms.control: X1's features [cross-encoder logit, log1p km, LGA agree, coordinates missing], refitted on the development labels
arms.level: control plus the facility-level weight of evidence (level_woe, keyed by |GRID3 facility_level - HFR type| over Primary/Secondary/Tertiary; unknown scores 0)
arms.reference: match-everything, scored under the same rule; it must fail for the rule to mean anything

rule.development: every label read before this file, corrected by the recheck: the 2026-08-19 and X1 packs' corrected copies and the near-miss pack (692 labelled pairs)
rule.error_bound: errors among auto-decided <= 3% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 10%
rule.false_merge_bound: different pairs auto-matched / all different pairs <= 2% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%
rule.informative: void unless the test holds at least 60 different pairs
rule.level_helps: the level arm passes; on every seed it auto-matches no more different pairs than control; and the pair-bootstrap 95% lower bound of (level coverage - control coverage), each pair's coverage averaged over the 3 seeds, is above 0
rule.pass: informative, and every one of the 3 seeds meets fewer_held, error_bound and false_merge_bound
rule.population: the X3 pack (data/review_packs/nigeria_facilities_x3_2026-11-22, 180 pairs, 60 per state in Edo, Kano and Ondo: 20 lookalike, 20 near_miss, 20 drift each) marked same_entity or different; read once, after this file
secondary: results by pair kind (lookalike, near_miss, drift)
rule.thresholds: x0.thresholds (FPR <= 1% above hi, FNR <= 1% below lo) applied to 5-fold out-of-fold development predictions (fold = sha256('x3', decision_id) mod 5); weights then fitted on all development rows

test.blind: the reviewer sees neither the engine's decision nor the pair's kind
test.construction: data/scripts/build_x3_pack.py: lookalike = closest-named HFR record in another LGA within 50 km (cosine >= 0.5), not the GRID3 facility's own; near_miss = closest-named HFR record in the same LGA (cosine >= 0.35), not its own; drift = its own HFR record when the names differ (trigram cosine < 0.8); no record from any earlier pack; each row shows decision 'review', no score, and the GRID3 facility's own HFR record

why: NPHCDA defines facility types by level of care; on 38,573 training-state twins sharing a source id the two registries' levels agree 92.8% of the time and are two levels apart 0.25% of the time, against 2.2% between a facility and a random other one in its LGA. Within primary care, names such as health post, dispensary and PHC are not evidence; the level fields are structured and come from the registries
